Trump Pushes ‘Lock the Clock’ Agenda
On Saturday, in a
Truth Social
post, Trump said Cotton, "a friend of mine," was "holding up a very important Bill" and accused the Republican senator of holding up the Sunshine Protection Act in the Senate
"For some reason, Tom is stopping the Bill," he said, urging Arkansas residents to tell Cotton to "GET IT DONE!"

"To the Great People of Arkansas, please let your Senator know it would be a GREAT Bipartisan WIN for the United States Senate, and for America itself. Call Tom on his cellphone at… and let him know," he added.
The President argued that Americans prefer more daylight later in the day, writing that "having sunshine in the afternoon is better than early in the morning."
He cited the PGA Tour, saying it "needs more Daylight in the afternoon in order to finish their Tournaments."
He also pointed to "regular Golfers, Tennis Players, Hunters and, perhaps most importantly, Farmers" who could benefit from additional afternoon daylight.
Trump said "65% PLUS want more sun in the afternoon" while "100% don’t want to change their Clocks twice a year." He said Americans want to "LOCK THE CLOCK!"
He also noted that the House passed the measure by a 308-117 vote and demanded, "HAVE THE SENATE VOTE, NOW!"

Trump Pushes Permanent DST
In August, Trump urged the Senate to pass the Sunshine Protection Act "ASAP,"
"foolish, inconvenient and, in some cases, very costly."
He argued that permanent daylight saving time could improve safety, health and economic activity.
